title: Aero engine
object: Flat-four, air-cooled, direct-drive aircraft piston engine in plan section through all four cylinders, with a section through one cylinder's valve train
idea: Four opposed cylinders sharing one crank: smooth, balanced power with redundant ignition
summary: A 5.24 L flat-four, the engine of a four-seat light aircraft. Opposed pistons move out and in together on throws 180° apart, so their forces cancel; the cylinders fire 1-3-2-4, one power stroke every half turn. A computed cycle at 2,700 rpm sets each cylinder's gas and its torque on the crank, and two magnetos fire two plugs in every cylinder.
usedFor: Aviation maintenance and pilot training: how the engine in front of the panel works
Engineering courses: multi-cylinder balance, firing order, torque ripple, air cooling
A software-concept explainer: redundancy (two independent ignition systems) and staggered work (a firing order spreads load evenly)
